chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ismail ibn Muhammad al-Minqari, from Hisham al-Saydalani who said:
Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Hisham! Even if you see the two battle lines having met, do not abandon seeking your livelihood on that day.'

key_terms.الرِّزْق: rizq — divinely apportioned sustenance; in Islamic theology, God is Al-Razzaq (the Provider), and seeking rizq is an act of trust in God's provision
key_terms.الصَّفَّيْنِ: the two battle lines — a vivid hyperbole representing the most extreme and dangerous of circumstances, meant to emphasize that even in such conditions the pursuit of livelihood must not stop
key_terms.طَلَبَ الرِّزْقِ: seeking the livelihood/sustenance — the active pursuit of one's means of earning, understood in Islamic tradition as a meritorious religious act

ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Sadiq teach that one must keep working even during war or battle?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (as) addresses his companion Hisham al-Saydalani with an emphatic teaching: even in the most extreme circumstances imaginable — the midst of a battle with two armies clashing — a Muslim must not abandon the pursuit of lawful sustenance. The teaching reflects the Islamic view that earning one's livelihood is a religious duty, not merely a worldly concern. For Hisham, a pharmacist and trusted companion, this instruction underscored that commercial and productive activity is so sacred that even war cannot be used as a pretext to neglect it.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ismail Bin Muhammad Al Minqary, from Hisham Al Saydalany who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Hisham! Even if you were to see the two swords having met (in battle), so do not leave seeking the livelihood during that day’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Isma’il ibn Muhammad al-Minqariy from Hisham al- Saydalaniy who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said to me, £ 0 Hisham, even if you find yourself in the two armies facing each other to fight, you must not neglect working for your sustenance on such day.’”
